summary.name: Mixed-Media Animation. This normalized label does not establish that physical stop-motion footage was used.
summary.visualIdentity: Shared color, line, texture, and lighting rules are set before mixing photos, drawings, paper, type, or 3D objects. Each medium takes a narrative role and links to others through composition, direction, and intentional transitions. Medium differences are kept within one coherent whole.
summary.suitableUses: Listed good fits are product and editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Inferred from the hybrid suggestions: documentary-style brand stories and research summaries built from supplied photos and sketches.
summary.limitations: Adapt or omit when the topic is too short for chapter boundaries, when transitions obscure causality, or when a cut violates a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over images or video. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production.
summary.palette: Reference-dependent example, not a canonical style palette: background #F1E6D1, foreground #3B4948, accent_1 #688E87, accent_2 #B97A5C. Task, brand, or source colors override these and must be preserved. Gradients are disabled, so use discrete tokens. Background and foreground reach 7.605:1, while accents fall below 4.5:1 against the background, so they are decorative only.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is organized into chapters. Optional catalog references are progress-linked chapter handoffs (motion-012), narrative steps with reading holds (motion-015), and a glitch cut (motion-020) only for intentionally disrupted tone. Video uses composition time, while scroll applies only to interactive delivery. Direct, reverse, and out-of-order seeks must match.
summary.audio: The style does not prescribe audio. Options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience, or silence, chosen per topic and audience. Honor any explicit user or supplied audio first. Do not default to instrumental music or invent audio assets. Verify speech intelligibility, balance, absence of clipping, and picture sync.
summary.assetRequirements: Photographs, drawings, and paper need preprocessing for consistent color, edges, and dimensions. 3D elements should be prerendered as transparent sequences before compositing with text and images. Crops need motion overscan and preserved source files. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Missing assets must be reported, not invented.
summary.combinations: Use this style alone when supplied media already share visual rules. Suggested hybrid style-024 adds handwritten annotations in approved tokens that appear after the medium they describe. Suggested hybrid style-101 adds restrained layered parallax with small offsets and one light direction. Avoid retinting supplied photos or mismatched per-layer motion directions.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export, with a paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limit applies, and the reason must be recorded. Visuals belong to the style renderer (PixiJS or Rough.js where appropriate), and motion belongs to one engine per property. Python/Pillow or Sharp handle preprocessing.
